chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a female slave while she is pregnant, does he have intercourse with her? He said, 'No.' I said, 'And what is below the vulva?' He said, 'He should not approach her.' His saying (peace be upon him) 'He should not approach her' regarding what is below the vulva is to be understood as referring to the dislike (karahah) that we have previously mentioned, rather than prohibition (haram), and that which also reveals this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sexual intimacy with a pregnant female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction is made between the prohibition of full intercourse (dakhil) and the permissibility of other sexual contact (dun al-farj) with a pregnant slave girl, which is classified as makruh rather than haram. This ruling highlights the specific juristic nuances in Shia fiqh regarding the physical well-being of the fetus and the rights of the owner, distinguishing between absolute prohibition and recommended caution.
